explication:
<explanation>
1. Project type and purpose  
   - This is an open-source, monolithic CLI tool written in Go (the Cloud Foundry CLI).  
   - It implements two major versions (v7 and v8) of Cloud Foundry API clients, a plugin API, command parsing, and local configuration/state persistence.

2. High-level architectural layers  
   A useful way to break the system into components for your diagram is by layering it as follows:  
   a. Presentation / Entrypoint  
      • main.go → CLI initialization, reads flags, invokes the command loader  
      • command loader / parser (cf/commandsloader, cf/flagcontext, util/command_parser)  
   b. Command Registry & Handlers  
      • cf/commandregistry & cf/commands/v7 + cf/commands (core commands)  
      • Implements the Command Pattern: each command is a struct with `Execute()`  
   c. Actor Layer (Business Logic)  
      • actor/sharedaction: reusable plumbing (auth, help, target checking)  
      • actor/v7action & actor/v7pushaction: core push/poll/start/stop logic against CF API  
      • actor/pluginaction: install/uninstall plugins  
      • actor/cfnetworkingaction: network policy operations  
   d. API Client Layer  
      • api/cloudcontroller (v2 & ccv3), api/uaa, api/router, api/logcache, api/plugin  
      • Wrap raw HTTP, handle authentication, versioning, error conversion  
   e. Transport & Helpers  
      • cf/net & api/*/wrapper: HTTP client, retries, trace headers, request logging  
   f. Configuration & Persistence  
      • cf/configuration & util/configv3: read/write ~/.cf/config.json, plugin configs  
      • manifest & .cfignore parsing (cf/manifest, util/manifestparser)  
   g. Output / UI  
      • cf/terminal: tables, color, prompts  
      • cf/trace: logging/tracing to stdout or file  
      • i18n: localization via JSON resource files  
   h. Plugins Subsystem  
      • plugin/shim & plugin/rpc: RPC‐based plugin protocol, `cf plugin install`  
      • plugin/cli_connection: in‐process plugin invocation  
   i. External Systems  
      • Cloud Foundry CC API endpoints (v2/v3), UAA auth, Routing API, Log Cache  
      • Local disk for config and plugin binaries  
      • SSH subsystem (cf/ssh, util/clissh)  

3. Relationships & data flow  
   - User → Terminal → main.go → command parser → command registry  
   - From a command `Execute()` → Actor layer (shared / v7 / plugin actor)  
   - Actors call API Client layer → HTTP Transport → Cloud Foundry back-end services  
   - Responses flow back up: HTTP → API client → Actor → Command → UI → User  
   - Configuration reads/writes happen at startup or by specific commands (e.g., `cf config`)  
   - Plugin commands are discovered/loaded at startup; calls go through shim → RPC server → plugin process  

4. Architectural patterns & principles  
   - Command Pattern for extensible CLI commands  
   - Actor (Service) Layer to encapsulate business logic, isolate from HTTP details  
   - Adapter/Wrapper around HTTP clients for retry, auth, trace  
   - Plugin API via RPC for external extension  
   - Strict separation of concerns: parsing, business logic, transport, UI, config  

5. Technologies & frameworks  
   - Go modules (go.mod), standard library + minimal external deps  
   - ginkgo/gomega for testing (numerous `_test.go` suites)  
   - JSON‐based i18n and CLI‐help templates  
   - Makefile, GitHub Actions workflows for build/test/release  

6. Guidelines for tailoring the diagram  
   - Emphasize separation between:  
     • CLI core (parsing + registry)  
     • Business logic (actors)  
     • API clients (cloudcontroller, uaa, router, logcache, plugin)  
     • Transport/helpers (network wrappers)  
     • UI/presentation (terminal, trace)  
     • Configuration storage (local disk, manifests)  
     • Plugin subsystem (shim, RPC)  
   - Show external systems as distinct icons (e.g., “Cloud Controller API”, “UAA Auth”)  
   - Clearly label v7 vs v8 command packages if relevant  

7. Diagramming best practices  
   - Use boxes/rectangles for each component group, color-code by layer:  
     * Blue = CLI core & parser  
     * Green = Actor/business logic  
     * Orange = API clients  
     * Purple = Plugins  
     * Grey = Config & util  
   - Use a cylinder icon for configuration storage on disk  
   - Use cloud icons for external CF services  
   - Draw directional arrows for data flow:  
     * User → CLI → Actors → API client → External service  
     * Responses back the same path  
   - Annotate high-level protocols (HTTP/REST, RPC, file I/O) along the arrows  
   - Include a legend for shapes, colors, and arrow styles  

By decomposing the CLI into these layers and components, your system design diagram will clearly express how commands flow from user input through parsing, business logic, HTTP transport, and back, while also showing the plugin extension points and configuration subsystems. Keep every box labeled, arrows directional, and color coding consistent to maximize clarity.
